content.overview: In a winding up, subject to section 326, specified debts (government dues, limited employee wages/salary, accrued holiday remuneration, ESI contributions, workmen’s compensation, employee welfare fund sums, and investigation expenses) are paid in priority to all other debts. They rank equally among themselves and, if assets are insufficient, abate rateably; they also have priority over floating-charge holders to the extent general assets are insufficient.
content.glance: Preferential debts (tax, limited wages, holiday pay, ESI, compensation, welfare funds, investigation costs) rank after s. 326 overriding preferences and before ordinary unsecured creditors.
content.study: Section 327 lists the preferential payments that follow the overriding preferential payments of section 326. The list covers revenues/taxes/cesses/rates due within twelve months before the relevant date; wages or salary for a period not exceeding four months within that year (subject to a notified ceiling for workmen); accrued holiday remuneration; employer ESI (or analogous) contributions for the preceding twelve months (except pure reconstruction/amalgamation voluntary winding up); workmen’s compensation liabilities (subject to insurance transfer rights); sums due from employee welfare funds maintained by the company; and expenses of investigations under sections 213 and 216 payable by the company. Sub-section (2) gives a priority right to a person who advanced money to pay such wages or holiday remuneration. Preferential debts rank equally and abate proportionately if assets are short; they also enjoy priority over floating-charge claims when general assets are insufficient. They must be discharged promptly (subject to retention for winding-up costs). Goods distrained within three months before a winding-up order are subject to a first charge for these preferential debts. Holiday or sickness absence remuneration is treated as wages. The section does not apply to IBC liquidations (see s. 327(7) inserted by the IBC).

sections.heading: Preferential list (subject to s. 326)
sections.body: Government and local-authority dues (12-month window); limited employee wages/salary (≤4 months within 12 months, notified ceiling for workmen); accrued holiday remuneration; ESI/employer contributions (12 months); workmen’s compensation liabilities; employee welfare-fund sums; investigation expenses under ss. 213/216.

sections.heading: Ranking and priority over floating charge
sections.body: Preferential debts rank equally among themselves and abate rateably if assets are insufficient. They have priority over floating-charge holders to the extent the assets available for general creditors are insufficient.

sections.heading: Relevant date and IBC carve-out
sections.body: Relevant date is the date of appointment of provisional liquidator or winding-up order (Tribunal cases) or the voluntary winding-up resolution date. Sections 326 and 327 do not apply in an IBC liquidation; IBC s. 53 governs distribution there.

examples.title: Tax and wage priority
examples.body: In a Tribunal winding up, unpaid GST for the twelve months before the relevant date and four months’ unpaid salary of an employee (within the notified ceiling) are preferential under s. 327 and are paid after any s. 326 overriding claims but before ordinary unsecured creditors.

examples.title: Floating-charge interaction
examples.body: If general assets are insufficient to meet preferential debts, those debts may be paid out of property subject to a floating charge in priority to the charge-holder’s claims under s. 327(3)(b).

hypotheticals.question: Are four months’ unpaid wages preferential in a Companies Act winding up?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, subject to the twelve-month window, the notified ceiling for a workman, and ranking after any s. 326 overriding preferential payments. Formal proof rules and the IBC carve-out must also be checked.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 327 apply in an IBC liquidation?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 327(7) (inserted by the IBC) provides that sections 326 and 327 do not apply in an IBC liquidation; distribution follows IBC s. 53 (subject to s. 36(4)).

rows.right: Workmen’s dues and limited secured-creditor residual

misconceptions.trap: All employee wages are preferential without limit.
misconceptions.correction: Only wages/salary for a period not exceeding four months within the twelve months before the relevant date, and for a workman subject to the notified ceiling.

misconceptions.trap: Section 327 applies unchanged in every liquidation, including under the IBC.
misconceptions.correction: Section 327(7) excludes application of ss. 326 and 327 in an IBC liquidation; IBC s. 53 governs.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 327 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the relevant date and the list of preferential debts. II. Apply the time windows and ceilings. III. Rank after s. 326 and before ordinary unsecured (and check floating-charge priority). IV. Note the IBC carve-out if applicable.

examTips: Name the preferential categories and the twelve-month / four-month limits.
State the ranking relative to s. 326 and floating charges.
revisionPoints: Priority over floating charge when general assets insufficient
